7-civ.3: Each generation is promised that the next invention will finally set it free.
7-civ.4: A society that tries to unplug is pulled back by work, school and family all online.

7-civ.6: A culture is told it is more connected than ever while loneliness keeps rising.
7-civ.7: People must live online to work and belong, then are blamed for being addicted.
7-civ.8: A whole society checks its phones in waves, waiting for the next small reward.
7-civ.9: The promise of progress moves forward with every release and never arrives.
7-civ.10: Words like "innovation" and "disruption" excuse almost anything technology does.
7-civ.11: Societies blame young people's phones for problems the adult world built into them.
7-civ.12: Critics of the technology are called afraid of progress and left behind.
7-civ.13: A generation grows up thinking constant tracking is simply how life works.
7-civ.14: Neighbors live side by side and talk only through screens.
7-civ.15: Whole nations measure their lives against a stream of curated perfection.
7-civ.16: Ordinary people defend the platforms that profit from their attention.
7-civ.17: Anyone who questions the digital world is mocked as out of touch.
7-civ.18: A culture stops talking about the cost of screens as if silence settles it.
7-civ.19: Society accepts surveillance as the fair price of convenience.
7-civ.20: A culture feels anxious without the devices that made it anxious.
7-civ.21: People come to believe no one can live without the platforms anymore.
7-civ.22: Tech leaders present control of the information supply as a service to humanity.
7-civ.23: Adults are treated as users who need to be nudged rather than citizens who choose.
7-civ.24: Human identity shrinks into usernames, followers and scores.
7-civ.25: A culture calls endless screen use a personal choice and avoids the deeper reckoning.
7-civ.26: Whole economies depend on a handful of companies that hold everyone's data.
7-civ.27: Each new tech panic is used to sell the next product as the cure.
7-civ.28: Skills that once held communities together are discarded as obsolete.
7-civ.29: Each generation of devices replaces the last, and the old ones pile up as waste.
7-civ.30: No one person designed the attention economy, so no one has to answer for it.
